analysis.summary: Found inconsistent AWS API response handling between GET and POST/DELETE endpoints, and missing validation for new required authentication tokens.

bugs.title: Inconsistent AWS API response structure handling
bugs.description: Code still accesses `.output?.product` in response, but AWS API returns flat structure like GET endpoint (which was updated to remove `.output`)
bugs.risk: Will always return undefined for product, causing isProductInGarage to be false even when product exists
bugs.codeSnippet:
const productInGarage = response?.[`response-data`]?.output?.product;
    const isProductInGarage = Boolean(productInGarage?.code === productId);

bugs.title: Inconsistent AWS API response structure handling
bugs.description: Code still accesses `.output?.product` in response, but AWS API returns flat structure without `.output` wrapper (as shown in GET migration)
bugs.risk: Will always return undefined for product, causing isProductInGarage to be false even when product was successfully added
bugs.codeSnippet:
const productInGarage = response?.[`response-data`]?.output?.product;
    const isProductInGarage = Boolean(productInGarage?.code === productId);

bugs.title: Missing validation for required idToken and accessToken
bugs.description: fetchDeleteGarage requires idToken and accessToken (string types) but caller doesn't validate they exist before passing userDetails.idToken/userDetails.accessToken
bugs.risk: If tokens missing from cookie, undefined values sent as headers causing AWS API authentication failures or runtime TypeError

notBugs.reason: speculative - may be intentional reuse of HTTP client logic; no evidence of runtime failure in diff

notBugs.topic: PN18 to pn18 query param case change
notBugs.reason: intentional migration change to match AWS API contract

notBugs.topic: baseSiteId and userId moved from query to headers
notBugs.reason: intentional API contract change for AWS migration, consistent across all three endpoints
